newsitem.title: FRANCE: French MEP hits out at European Parliament vote.
newsitem.headline: French MEP hits out at European Parliament vote.

text.p: Spanish conservative Jose Maria Gil Robles was widely believed to be set for election as President of the European Parliament when deputies vote on Tuesday.

But the woman standing as a protest candidate, France's Catherine Lalumiere, said on Monday the EU's directly-elected assembly risked alienating the citizens it was trying to win over by what she called undemocratic election methods.
Under a deal between the parliament's two big groups -- the Socialists and the European People's Party (PPE) -- each holds the presidency for half the parliament's five-year legislature.

The choice of the PPE president who will chair the assembly as it seeks new powers in the closing stages of the EU's intergovernmental conference, came down to a deal between its two biggest national delegations Germany and Spain.

France's Lalumiere, former Council of Europe Secretary General and leader of the assembly's alternative European Radical Alliance, said she was not standing in Tuesday's vote with any illusion that she would win.
She was rather responding to widespread protest at the carve-up between the two big groups, which had determined the election for the past six years.
"The practice that rules inside the European Parliament is such that my chances of success are zero," she told a news conference. "I am perfectly realistic, aware of the situation."
She said "15 countries of the Union can see the ball bounce back from one country to another, and 13 countries are excluded and transformed into spectators."

The backstage division of top jobs also extends to the positions of vice president, the five quaestors who oversee deputies' interests and spending, and the chairmanship of more than 20 parliamentary committees, which scrutinise and amend draft EU legislation.

Gil Robles, a 61-year-old lawyer, is a member of Spain's ruling Popular Party (PP) and has been a Euro-MP since 1989. He is a son of Jose Maria Gil Robles who founded the Spanish Confederation of Autonomous Rights and was a war minister before the 1936-39 Civil War.
